predecessors.name: Scandinavian minor kingdoms
predecessors.text: Jutland and the Danish islands, the Danish part of the minor kingdoms before Gorm 'reigning from c.

predecessors.name: Kingdom of Germany
predecessors.text: Schleswig round Hedeby, which Cliopatria gives to Denmark in 936

successors.name: Kalmar Union
successors.text: Denmark inside the union of Denmark, Norway and Sweden, 'Incorporated into the Kalmar Union: 17 June 1397'

rulers.name: Cnut the Great
rulers.title: king of Denmark, England and later Norway

ledger.x: 936: Gorm the Old reigns from Jelling and the Danish kingdom begins.
960: Scania, Halland and Blekinge pass to the Danish crown in Cliopatria.

c. 970: Harald Bluetooth rules Norway as well as Denmark. Infobox 'Norway c. 970 - c. 985/986', the Jelling inscription says he 'won the whole of Denmark and Norway', with Haakon Sigurdsson as de facto ruler; the lead says the rule lasted 'no more than a few years in the 970s'. The year is c. 970; the Norwegian cells…
974: Otto II takes Hedeby and the Danevirke.
983: Harald regains part of the lost frontier.

c. 986: the Danish seat moves from Jelling to Roskilde. The History of Denmark infobox gives 'Jelling (until 10th cent.)' and 'Roskilde (since 10th cent.)'; the Sweyn Forkbeard page: 'The main centres of Danish power shifted from Jutland to the towns of Roskilde and Lund' (undated). The year is the bridge to Sweyn's…
995: the Danish overlordship of Norway lapses.

c. 1000: Sweyn is overlord of Norway again. 'In 999 or 1000, Swein defeated Olaf at the naval Battle of Svold', and after it 'he appointed Hakon's sons, Erik Hakonsson (his son-in-law) and Swein Hakonarson to rule as jarls'. The page does not split Norway among the victors.
August 1013: Sweyn Forkbeard invades England.
3 February 1014: Sweyn dies at Gainsborough and the Danish hold on England ends.
1015: Norway leaves the Danish overlordship.
September 1015: Cnut lands at Sandwich.
Late 1015: Wessex submits to Cnut.
Autumn 1016: England north of the Thames goes to Cnut.
30 November 1016: Edmund dies and Cnut is king of all England.
30 November 1016: the rest of England, south of the Thames and London, comes to Cnut with Edmund's death.
1018: Cnut takes the Danish crown and the realm becomes the North Sea Empire.
12 November 1035: Cnut dies and Denmark has its own king again.
1040: Harthacnut joins England to Denmark.
1047: Magnus dies and Sweyn Estridsson is king of Denmark.
1168: Valdemar and Absalon subdue Rugen.
1185: Bogislaw I of Pomerania becomes Canute VI's vassal.
1180s: Mecklenburg comes under Danish control.
1201: Valdemar takes the field against the Holstein count.
1203: the fighting over Holstein and Lubeck ends in a Danish conquest.
1203: Holstein and Lubeck come under the Danish crown.
1216: Hamburg falls to Valdemar II.
15 June 1219: Danish rule is established in northern Estonia.
1223: the German war begins with the king's capture.
22 July 1227: the Battle of Bornhoved ends the Danish hold on north Germany.
22 July 1227: Holstein, Lubeck and Hamburg are lost at Bornhoved.
1227: Danish overlordship of the Wendish coast ends with Bornhoved.
1227: Danish overlordship of Pomerania ends with Bornhoved ('all of the Wendish lands and Pomerania' had been acknowledged as Danish about 1218, per the same page).
1325: the Rugian principality leaves the Danish tie.
1332: Scania passes to Sweden.
24 June 1340: Valdemar IV is acclaimed king and the kingdom re-forms.
1344: southern Jutland is held by the Danish Magnates in Cliopatria.
1344: North Friesland is recovered.
1346: Valdemar retakes Zealand.
1346: Estonia is sold.
1352: the southern-Jutland cells return to the Danish shape.
1360: Valdemar IV takes back Scania, Halland and Blekinge.
1361: Valdemar IV conquers Gotland.
17 June 1397: Denmark joins Norway and Sweden in the Kalmar Union.

wars.name: Otto II's invasion of Denmark
wars.outcome: Harald attacked Saxony in 973; Otto II counter-attacked in 974 and took Haithabu and the Dannevirke; Harald regained some of the seized territory in 983, after Otto II's defeat.

wars.name: Sweyn Forkbeard's conquest of England
wars.outcome: Sweyn was acknowledged king by December 1013 and died on 3 February 1014; the English recalled Aethelred and Cnut left.

wars.name: Cnut's conquest of England
wars.outcome: Wessex submitted late in 1015; after Assandun (18 October 1016) the land north of the Thames went to Cnut and, on Edmund's death on 30 November, the whole kingdom.

wars.name: Sweyn Estridsson's war with Harald Hardrada
wars.outcome: Harald sacked Hedeby in 1050 and Aarhus; Sweyn nearly died at the naval Battle of Nisa off Halland in 1062; 'Harald relinquished his claims to Denmark in 1064'.

wars.name: Danish conquest of Rugen
wars.outcome: Valdemar and Absalon gained a foothold on the southern Baltic shore; the principality became a Danish vassal until 1325.

wars.name: Canute VI's Pomeranian war
wars.outcome: Barbarossa demanded in 1184 that Canute acknowledge him as liege; Canute 'ordered two invasions of Pomerania and in 1185 forced Bogislaw to acknowledge Canute as his overlord'.

wars.name: Valdemar II's campaign in Holstein and Lubeck
wars.outcome: Stellau 1201, Holstein and Lubeck conquered in 1203 (lead: 1207); Hamburg conquered in 1216.

wars.name: Danish conquest of northern Estonia
wars.outcome: Danish rule established in Estonia in 1219 after the Battle of Lindanise (15 June 1219); a fortress ordered at Reval.

wars.name: Valdemar II's captivity and the Battle of Bornhoved
wars.outcome: Valdemar and his son abducted in 1223 by Count Henry I of Schwerin; Danish defeat at Molln in 1225; Bornhoved on 22 July 1227 'cemented the loss of Denmark's north German territories'.

wars.name: Valdemar IV's recovery of the kingdom
wars.outcome: North Friesland recovered in 1344, Vordingborg and all Zealand in 1346, Helsingborg given up by Magnus in 1360.

wars.name: Danish conquest of Gotland
wars.outcome: Valdemar IV invaded Gotland in 1361 and took the title 'King of the Goths' (1361-1375).

wars.name: Danish-Hanseatic war
wars.outcome: 'In 1362 the Hansa states, Sweden, and Norway allied against Valdemar'; he left Denmark at Easter 1368 and 'was forced to sign the Treaty of Stralsund in 1370'.

certainty.note: Viking-Age and Valdemarian frontiers are approximate: the Schleswig border (Hedeby, Dannevirke), Scania and the Norwegian and English holdings; the pages give no survey or treaty line.
After Bornhoved the frontier follows the Eider and the sea; the pages give no treaty line (the Treaty of Stralsund, 1370, is not described).
